title: Archive every attempt's report; a superseded attempt's analysis is lost with its worktree
description:
From the ticks pwp run, 2026-09-15 (close-out tick 8vl, attempt 15 — reported by the worker about its own predecessors).

Attempts 11-14 each wrote a closeout report at the prescribed worktree path. Only attempt 11's was captured anywhere (decisions/3.json). The reports of 12, 13 and 14 survive nowhere in the repository; their reasoning is recoverable only from the findings they happened to file.

This is why the closeout loop was expensive as well as stuck. Each re-dispatched attempt started blind, re-derived the same situation from the tick's notes, and surfaced a DIFFERENT subset of what it found — which is why five attempts produced five disjoint finding sets rather than converging. An attempt that could read its predecessors' reports would have seen the work already done.

Fix: when the collect channel reads an attempt's report, archive it under the run's own .ticfac/ state (alongside attempts/<n>.json), whatever the verdict. A rejected or superseded attempt's analysis is evidence about the epic; losing it with the worktree throws away the most expensive artifact the run produced.

Relationship to 54n: 54n is why the closeout could not commit; this is why each retry was blind. Fixing 54n alone ends the loop; fixing this alone makes each retry cheaper and more convergent. They are independent.
notes:
2026-09-15 09:23 - PREMISE CORRECTED. The reports are NOT lost — the finding's wording ('survive nowhere in the repository') is true but misleading, and I repeated it in this tick's description.

Every attempt's report survives in the executor's own state root, outside the repository:

  ~/.ticfac/exec/local-subprocess/runs/epic-pwp/8vl/{11,12,13,14,15}/*/*/result.json

Each carries the full role_result: status, summary, result and the findings array. I read attempt 13's just now, after its worktree was gone. So the artifact outlives the worktree; what it does not do is reach the run's .ticfac/ records in the repo, where a re-dispatched attempt or a reviewer would look.

That makes this tick cheaper than written: the work is to COPY an existing artifact into the run's durable records at collect, not to capture something that was being destroyed. The acceptance stands as-is.

It also means the pwp closeout's five reports are still on disk and recoverable if anyone wants them.
acceptance_criteria: Every attempt's report is archived under the run's .ticfac/ state when collect reads it, whatever the verdict, and a re-dispatched attempt can read its predecessors' reports — proven by a test that rejects an attempt and asserts its report survives the worktree teardown
